title: ICC Trial Chamber III sets conduct for Duterte trial proceedings
summary: PRAGUE, Czech Republic - The International Criminal Court"s (ICC) Trial Chamber III has set the conduct of proceedings for its trial of former President Rodrigo Duterte, which will start on November…
byline: Andy Peñafuerte III, Jay-vee Marasigan Pangan

blocks.text: PRAGUE, Czech Republic – The International Criminal Court’s (ICC) Trial Chamber III has set the conduct of proceedings for its trial of former President Rodrigo Duterte, which will start on November 30.

Under the Chamber’s latest directions, the proceedings will begin with the reading of the charges of crimes against humanity to Duterte, as stated in the April 23 decision that confirmed those charges.
The Chamber will not read the specific incidents underlying the three counts to Duterte.
Following that, the Chamber will ask the former president if he understands the nature of the charges and give him the opportunity to enter a plea admitting or denying his guilt.
The opening statements will proceed with the following schedule:

items: Office of the Prosecution: 2 hours and 15 minutes
Common Legal Representatives of the Victims (CLRV): 1 hour and 30 minutes
Outline of the Defense’s case: 1 hour.

blocks.text: The first prosecution witness will testify immediately after the opening statements.
As confirmed by Trial Chamber III, daily hearings will have four one-hour blocks:
The opening block of the proceedings begins on November 30 and continues until the court’s judicial recess on December 18.
The Chamber has also set the hearings on evidence for the first four months of 2027:

The court said it would set the schedule of evidentiary blocks “in due course” after April 30. It also announced that no hearings would be held on February 22-26 for courtroom maintenance, as well as on January 19 and February 11.
Witness schedule, Rule 68 requests, materials, and transcripts
Trial Chamber III directed parties in the Duterte proceedings to provide a schedule of forthcoming witnesses no later than four weeks before each evidentiary block hearing.
It also expects the parties to organize their witnesses’ appearance schedules so no gaps occur during testimony and to inform the Registry if their order changes.

The court also set deadlines for responses to Rule 68(3) witnesses applied for by the prosecution, and directed the parties to indicate the electronic registration numbers (ERN) of the materials they intend to use when questioning witnesses.
The parties are also instructed to agree on spelling and coordinate with the Registry to ensure accurate court records, and to inform the court if they object to the requested redactions.

The chamber’s direction comes as the prosecution, the CLRV, the defense, and the Registry prepare for the trial of Duterte, the first Filipino and Asian leader to face the International Criminal Court. — BAP, GMA News
